web_evidence.title: Comanche Moon: A Novel by Larry McMurtry
web_evidence.note: A sustained licensed ebook extract spans multiple opening chapters and shifts among Call, Long Bill, Scull, Buffalo Hump, Blue Duck, and Augustus through third-person narration and interior access.

web_evidence.title: The Novel Writer’s Toolkit: A Guide to Writing Great Fiction and Getting It Published
web_evidence.note: The published writing guide explicitly uses Comanche Moon as an example of third-person shifting, explaining that McMurtry moves among characters’ third-person viewpoints, sometimes paragraph by paragraph.

web_evidence.title: Nothing Wrong: Law and the Contemporary American Western
web_evidence.note: A York University English dissertation analyzes the novel’s late action and explicitly identifies Blue Duck’s killing of Buffalo Hump as third-person narration before Gus and Call arrive, corroborating third person near the ending.

person_note: The Goodreads passages repeatedly show a nonparticipating narrator entering the minds of Buffalo Hump, Blue Duck, Famous Shoes, Augustus, and other characters in third person. All visible narratorial I/we forms are confined to dialogue, and no evidence indicates a sustained first- or second-person section. A sustained licensed opening extract independently displays shifting third-person viewpoints; a published writing guide explicitly identifies that technique across Comanche Moon, and scholarly analysis confirms third-person narration near the ending. The main limitation is that the authorized prose source covers the opening rather than the entire novel, but the structural and late-book evidence resolves that scope gap without credible contradiction.
